transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump's remarks that Iran should take out Los Angeles or San Diego are not sitting well with Democrats.
Congressman James Wonkinshaw sits on the House National Security Committee.
He says Trump should choose his words more carefully.
>> My immediate thought was there he goes again.
>> You know, I think it's something for effect in a rally, attempting to get an applause line, perhaps,
but it causes fear and anxiety for millions and millions of Americans.
>> The White House says the president was simply raising security concerns with a spokesman,
dismissing the criticism as a media freakout.
Trump made the comment at a rally in Nebraska Monday night,
drawing a swift rebuke from California's Democratic leaders and some Republicans.
>> President Trump announced his MAGA Inc. super PAC would start paying for controversial ads promoting his administration.
It was not clear what that would mean for the ads that had already aired.
NPR's Tamara Keith reports that's now coming into focus.
>> The White House insisted the ads were public service announcements meant to promote patriotism.
But lawmakers from both sides of the aisle criticized taxpayer dollars going to what looked like political advertisements.
On Monday, Trump announced MAGA Inc. would take over funding the ads.
But a White House official, not authorized to speak on the record,
confirmed that didn't mean the super PAC would reimburse taxpayers for the ads that have already aired.
According to Ad Impact, the US government has spent more than $11.5 million to air the ads nationwide.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
>> Krista Pike's attorneys say she is awake and speaking following her failed execution last week in Tennessee.
A statement from Pike's lawyers, the first indication that Pike's condition has improved after surviving two doses of a lethal injection drug.
Trump administration urging Russia to be more transparent about the death of the lab worker in Siberia last week in a suspected case of pneumonic plague.
NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports that the State Department says it's been in touch with Russia's foreign ministry since last Friday when the news first emerged.
>> Secretary of State Marco Rubio sounded frustrated with the lack of information.
But he wouldn't speculate when asked whether this could have been a leak of a strain of the plague that was altered by Russia.
>> I think it's incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world.
That's what they should do.
That's what we hope they will do.
And the more we can learn about what happened, the better all of us can be in a position of responding.
>> So far, it is State Department health experts who have been reaching out to Russia for information.
Though arms control experts have expressed concern that Russia maintains an offensive biological warfare program.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.
>> And you're listening to NPR News.
>> Federal authorities are charging a Washington State man with aiding and encouraging a school shooter in Canada.
They say 30-year-old James Cody Bryant of Bellingham communicated with the 18-year-old shooter for six months before the attack on a school in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia.
Authorities say Jesse Van Rudselar killed two family members at home before attacking the nearby school.
Six more people were killed and more than two dozen others were wounded.
Rudselar was later found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound.
>> Trustees at Cornell University bringing in a former top official at the Justice Department to review how the school handles sexual misconduct complaints.
They announced Tuesday that former Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates will conduct a review.
The announcement follows outrage on campus over allegations of a 2024 gang rape at a fraternity house.
The actress Eva Marie Saint has died at the age of 102.
The big screen star had leading roles in such classic films as On the Waterfront and North by Northwest, and PR's Colin Dwyer has more.
>> Back in 2014, exactly 60 years after the release of On the Waterfront, Eva Marie Saint told NPR she had no idea that they were making a classic.
>> Of course not. You just want to do the best you can. You take each day at a time.
I don't think anyone ever knows.
>> At the age of 30, it was her first feature film, and she won an Oscar for it.
She went on to play the femme fatale in Alfred Hitchcock's North by Northwest.
And later in her career, in 1990, she won an Emmy for her TV work.
Colin Dwyer, NPR News.
>> This is NPR News.

topics.text: President Trump's remarks that Iran should attack Los Angeles or San Diego draw Democratic criticism
Trump's MAGA Inc. super PAC to fund controversial ads; $11.5 million already spent by government
Krista Pike awake and speaking after failed execution in Tennessee last week
Trump administration urges Russia to be transparent about death of lab worker in Siberia from suspected pneumonic plague
Federal authorities charge Washington State man with aiding Canadian school shooter who killed eight people
Cornell University hires former Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to review sexual misconduct complaint handling
Actress Eva Marie Saint dies at age 102; starred in On the Waterfront and North by Northwest
